notes:
PASSED on the fake backend only: `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/bnl-atf__ophyd-basler --backend fake` exited 0 on 2026-11-05 with G1 to G9 pass and no findings or warnings. The evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by is a model, reviewed_by is null); no human reviewed or tested it, no camera was attached, and no hardware run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper OphydDriver (family ophyd) and candidate class cap.device.configure.v1. The entry symbol was confirmed at ophyd_basler/basler_camera.py:21. The package is a direct Driver, not OphydDriver, because OphydDriver compiles only classic Signal get/set bindings and cannot express the native stage -> grab_image -> unstage capture, the pylon StopGrabbing stop, or the image artifact. No native method or wire syntax was changed. cap.device.configure.v1 is bound by the exposure_time write and cap.sensing.image.v1 by the capture action; no extension ids were used, so there are no catalogue_requests.

MOCK PATH: the card prefers a fake. The upstream tests set PYLON_CAMEMU and use the pylon emulated camera (ophyd_basler/tests/test_emulated_camera.py:15-43), which still needs pypylon and the Basler runtime. The package fake is a source-shaped in-memory stand-in for BaslerCamera with the same public attributes and only the root methods the driver calls (stage, grab_image, unstage); it imports no pypylon, ophyd or upstream code. It is not a recording and returns an 8 x 8 placeholder frame; the real frame shape is the image_shape read. The upstream test's 1040 x 1024 expectation is test configuration, not a device bound.

NOT COVERED: the optional cap.sensing.image.v1 width, height, exposure_ms and format inputs are not served; the upstream class exposes no documented resolution or pixel-format setter for them, and exposure is the separate exposure_time write that the next capture applies through stage. set_custom_images (emulation-only configuration), trigger (the ophyd plan integration that also writes the HDF5 dataset), collect_asset_docs, the image datum-id signal, available_devices and collect_asset_docs are not exposed. The capture publishes a lossless PNG through the endpoint-owned artifact store; the store's per-artifact bound applies (the SDK default is 2 MiB, and a larger frame needs an explicit store bound). The driver refuses a frame outside 1..8192 pixels per side and a frame that is not a two-dimensional Mono image; color or non-Mono pixel formats are not covered. The upstream stage creates an HDF5 file under root_dir/YYYY/MM/DD and expects that directory tree to exist (the upstream test creates it with ophyd make_dir_tree); the hardware factory forwards root_dir but does not create it.

UNITS AND LIMITS: exposure_time is milliseconds (basler_camera.py:24). The clone states no numeric exposure range; stage reads ExposureTimeAbs.Min and ExposureTimeAbs.Max from the connected camera and clamps to them (basler_camera.py:237-263), so the write is Limit.operator_required and site-limits.example.json is an illustrative narrowing overlay, not a device fact. The source's exposure and grab-timeout Signal values are constructor defaults and are not used as Limits. image_shape, pixel levels, payload size and grab timeout are reads; width and height in the capture output are the actual returned array shape.

SAFETY: the declared risk is R1 (the card floor; a camera is not a laser, robot, pump, heater or centrifuge). The @estop calls the pylon camera_object.StopGrabbing (basler_camera.py:158) and the runtime latches commands. Safe state: the current grab is stopped, the camera object remains open and no further frame is requested. The clone documents no independent hardware emergency stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set and no physical e-stop protection is claimed. The loader's unreviewed-model hardware refusal covers R2 and R3, not this R1 package, so the absence of a hardware run is stated rather than protected by that refusal.

DEPLOYMENT: the hardware backend factory is .native:connect, which imports ophyd_basler.basler_camera and constructs BaslerCamera with the operator's options. A live run needs pypylon and the Basler pylon runtime, a camera visible to the pylon transport layer, and a writable root_dir with the current date tree; the configured exposure is applied by the native stage. None of this was run. No network access, package installation or upstream import was used while authoring.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation (OphydDriver binds Signal get/set only; the frame goes out as a PNG artifact, which a direct Driver supports, so the SDK change the readiness evidence asked for is not needed), every read and fact against basler_camera.py, the operator_required exposure limit, and StopGrabbing, the evidence's open item: it is the call grab_image itself makes (basler_camera.py:158) and an acceptable acquisition stop for this R1 camera (configure floor, no actuator). Defects: safe_state said the camera stays open, but the upstream closes it outside a capture (94, 266); the stage fact said the clamped exposure is applied, but an out-of-range request only corrects the Signal and nothing is written in that call (243-263); a fact carried a 'so' inference. The reviewer rewrote safe_state, corrected those facts and added two (stage opens a new HDF5 file in mode 'x' under a dated directory with a NaN first frame, 196-227; the upstream fixture creates that directory, conftest.py:37-38) in driver.py, facts.md and the native.py docstring, and regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md; gate and strict collector pass, digest unchanged (sha256:94c7c36ca117e690f77ebb471d7aa280bc5582bbd496c436c45cc2f1d34a5c1e). For the human reviewer: Each capture calls stage, which fails unless the dated root_dir/YYYY/MM/DD directory exists and leaves one HDF5 file with a NaN frame per capture (the driver never calls trigger); an out-of-range exposure takes effect only on the following capture. What StopGrabbing does while RetrieveResult waits in another thread, or on a closed camera, is pylon behaviour outside the clone. R1 only because of the exposure write; the camera has no physical hazard.
